mentions.author: Someone
mentions.story: Game Boy Wordle clone: How to compress 12972 five-letter words to 17871 bytes
mentions.text:
My first thought would be “DAWG”. That’s a smart way to represent a trie, with identical ‘tail’ ends of the trie merged into one.

[course] compresses a 780k word list into 175k. That’s about 22% of the size. This accomplishes 27%.

This list is a lot shorter, so there will be fewer opportunities for savings. On the other hand, all words are five letters, so the ‘is a word’ bit can be taken out.

No, actually it does rely on deterministically placed elements. And its analyzing unix qsort which is a deterministic algorithm.

Unless I'm misunderstanding the paper (which I could be).

The argument relies on the fact that the adversary can choose the elements on the fly. This requires the input be deterministic so that the adversary knows what elements are where. If you randomize the input, the adversary will have no knowledge of the input and thus is not able to choose which elements go in which index. This would be randomly generated.

For more information on the adversarial method see:
[course]

Recitation 09/08 explains this problem in depth.
